Genesis Chiropractic

Nobody warned me about this part.

The apps told me my baby was the size of an eggplant. Nobody mentioned I'd need a strategy just to roll over in bed — or that I'd build a pillow fortress every night and still wake up at 2 a.m. with my hip on fire.

When I finally asked about the pain, I got a kind smile and five words: "That's just part of pregnancy."

But at midnight, when the house is quiet and my hip is screaming, the real questions come out: If it hurts this much now, what will 38 weeks feel like? Is there anything that actually helps — and is it safe?

Here's the truth: pregnancy pain is real, it has a cause — and it is not something you're required to endure.

I'm Dr. Tiffani Fries, and I've spent the last 25 years caring for pregnant mamas as a Webster Certified prenatal chiropractor. That means specific training and gentle, pregnancy-safe techniques for exactly what your body is going through — shifting posture, loosening ligaments, a pelvis working overtime. (And yes, a table with room for your belly.)

The mamas in my practice tell me they're sleeping again. Moving easier. Feeling like themselves — and walking into their births strong instead of depleted.

🤍 The $67 Prenatal Assessment — unhurried, gentle, and all about you:

✨ Thorough one-on-one consultation 🤰 Hands-on postural, pelvic & Webster Technique exam — the prenatal-specific evaluation of your pelvic balance & alignment 🌿 Your first gentle adjustment 📋 A pregnancy care plan made just for you

PLUS Dr. Fries' Prenatal Comfort Collection to take home: 🧘‍♀️ Pregnancy-safe stretches for all trimesters 🥗 Dr. Fries' favorite nourishing meals for energy and a growing baby 😴 Sleep tips & tricks for getting comfortable at night — and finally getting a good night's rest

Pregnancy is a season you don't get back. You deserve to feel good enough to actually live it.

Tap below to claim your voucher and schedule your quick call — we'll learn about your pregnancy, answer your questions, and save your spot. Because prenatal visits get extra time with Dr. Fries, we only take a few new expecting moms each week.

offer","cards":[],"body":{"text":"Nobody warned me about this part.

The apps told me my baby was the size of an eggplant. Nobody mentioned I'd need a strategy just to roll over in bed — or that I'd build a pillow fortress every night and still wake up at 2 a.m. with my hip on fire.

When I finally asked about the pain, I got a kind smile and five words: "That's just part of pregnancy."

But at midnight, when the house is quiet and my hip is screaming, the real questions come out: If it hurts this much now, what will 38 weeks feel like? Is there anything that actually helps — and is it safe?

Here's the truth: pregnancy pain is real, it has a cause — and it is not something you're required to endure.

I'm Dr. Tiffani Fries, and I've spent the last 25 years caring for pregnant mamas as a Webster Certified prenatal chiropractor. That means specific training and gentle, pregnancy-safe techniques for exactly what your body is going through — shifting posture, loosening ligaments, a pelvis working overtime. (And yes, a table with room for your belly.)

The mamas in my practice tell me they're sleeping again. Moving easier. Feeling like themselves — and walking into their births strong instead of depleted.
